messages:
Maya C: Hey team — following the pager earlier, we need a concise customer-facing follow-up for the affected Dedicated customers. Draft below, please iterate.

Incident Bot: [ALERT] INC-2026-03-14-REDWOOD-INFERENCE: elevated latency and a subset of 503s on dedicated pools in us-west-2 (trigger 00:12 UTC).

Alex R (oncall): Quick summary: routing rules briefly picked a degraded quantized variant for 30m during peak, causing increased token latency and intermittent request timeouts. We rolled back routing at 00:45 UTC and scaled an extra pool at 00:50 UTC.

Sam P (engineer): Root cause initial analysis: kernel selection path picked legacy int8 runtime when hybrid fallback flag was on. That runtime had a cache eviction bug causing stalled KV cache reads under specific sequence distributions.

Lena T (support): Customer impact: 4 customers with Dedicated capacity (IDs redacted) experienced increased P99 latencies and short-lived 503s between ~00:12–00:45 UTC. No data exfiltration or model correctness issues. Customers reported user-facing timeouts and a couple opened support tickets.

Priya K (Product Ops): Drafting status page + email. Suggest we include exact timeline, what we fixed, mitigations, and follow-up actions + offer SLA credit language. Also include link to post-incident public RCA within 48h.

Maya C: Here's a first-pass customer email. Please keep it short and empathetic, and call out deterministic remediation steps. Edit inline.

Maya C (customer email draft):
Hi <Customer Team>,

We want to follow up on an incident that affected Dedicated inference throughput in the us-west-2 region on 2026-03-14 between ~00:12–00:45 UTC. During this window some requests experienced elevated latency and occasional timeouts.

What happened
- At ~00:12 UTC a routing configuration caused a subset of requests to be served by a degraded int8 runtime variant.
- This variant had a cache handling bug that under certain request patterns caused stalls and requests to time out.

What we did
- We reverted routing to the stable runtime at ~00:45 UTC.
- We provisioned additional capacity for the affected pools at ~00:50 UTC to absorb load.
- We monitored the fleet until metrics returned to normal and no further customer-facing errors were observed.

Impact
- A small number of requests served from Dedicated pools observed higher P99 latency and intermittent 503s. There was no data loss or model output corruption.

Next steps / prevention
- Patch the int8 runtime to fix KV cache eviction timing (deploy scheduled within 24h).
- Add an automatic routing health check to avoid switching to degraded runtime variants without a successful canary.
- Expand canary window + synthetic traffic during model rollouts.

We're committed to keeping your service reliable and will follow up with a concise post-incident report and the exact remediation timeline within 48 hours. If you'd like an SLA credit for the impacted window, reply and we'll prioritize that.

Sincerely,
Maya C, Customer Success on behalf of Redwood Inference

Alex R (oncall): Edits: change "small number of requests" to "a subset of requests". Add note: customers on Dedicated with pinned variants were unaffected unless they were routed to the degraded variant.

Sam P: Note for CS copy: we should avoid heavy technical jargon for some customers — remove 'KV' and say 'internal cache' in the external email.

Maya C: Updated email with that change.

Priya K: Status page update (short):
Status page entry: https://status.redwood.com/incidents/INC-2026-03-14-1
- Incident start: 2026-03-14 00:12 UTC
- Degraded routing variant introduced increased latency and intermittent timeouts for Dedicated customers in us-west-2.
- Mitigation: routing reverted at 00:45 UTC; additional capacity added at 00:50 UTC.
- Current status: Resolved. Post-incident report will be published within 48 hours.

Lena T: I'm going to notify the customers who opened tickets with the updated draft and link to the status page. I will include an opt-in for SLA credit.

Maya C: Also prepping an internal one-pager for Sales/Acct teams — short bullet points they can paste into customer messages. Draft below.

Maya C (internal one-pager):
- What happened: short routing change led to a degraded runtime variant serving some Dedicated traffic in us-west-2, causing elevated P99 latency and intermittent 503s from 00:12–00:45 UTC.
- Who was impacted: subset of Dedicated customers in us-west-2 (we will send list to reps).
- Action for AE/AM: proactively reach out to top 10 affected customers; offer call if they saw user-visible impact.
- Next steps: patch runtime; add canary checks; expand rollout automation.

Alex R: Action items for eng ops (I'll track):
- [ ] Emergency hotfix to runtime (Sam) — target deploy within 24h.
- [ ] Add routing health check (Alex/Sam) — RFC by EOD.
- [ ] Post-incident monitoring rule to surface early KV/cache stalls (Sam).
- [ ] Confirm list of impacted Dedicated customers and hand to CS (Lena).

Sam P: I'll push a hotfix branch now and start a test run against a local replica. If green, will coordinate with Alex for a canary deploy.

Incident Bot: [UPDATE] Incident marked resolved at 00:58 UTC.

Maya C: Final checklist before sending customer emails: 1) Confirm impacted customer list 2) Confirm patch schedule 3) Final review of email copy. Lena will do 1, Sam will confirm 2, and Priya will do review.

Lena T: I have the impacted list and I'll DM AE owners now.

Sam P: Patch build completed and smoke-tested in staging at 09:10 UTC. Planning canary deploy at 11:00 UTC PST.

Priya K: Reviewed final copy — approved. Sending to affected customers now. Will post status page update after sends.

Maya C: Sending note to customers. Will post the public post-incident summary in 24–48 hours with the full timeline and engineering RCA. Thanks everyone for the fast coordination.

Alex R: Leaving a final note for oncall handoff: ensure the routing health check alert is provided as part of next shift's runbook.

Maya C: Closing thread for now. If anything else actionable appears, please reopen.
